interludes.speaker: eng
interludes.text: Expanding the greenhouse by 25% takes 3 {Ds} of crew work, and the grow lights will drain power for good.
interludes.fact: Grow lights are one of the biggest power users on any space base.

interludes.speaker: sci

text.moon: Radar spotted possible ice in a crater a 2-day drive south. Send the rover?
text.mars: Radar shows ice under a dune field, a 4-sol drive away. Send the rover?

interludes.fact: Water ice gives drinking water, breathable oxygen, and even rocket fuel.

interludes.speaker: ops

text.moon: Solar flare alert! Radiation hits in hours. Shelter everyone for 2 days?
text.mars: Solar flare alert! Mars has no magnetic field to deflect it. Shelter for 2 sols?

interludes.fact: Astronauts shelter behind water tanks during flares, because water blocks radiation well.

text.moon: A ridge blocks our view of Earth. A relay satellite would fix it. 2 days to set up.
text.mars: Messages to Earth take up to 22 minutes. A bigger antenna would help. 3 sols to build.

fact.moon: Radio reaches the Moon in about 1.3 seconds, as long as nothing blocks the view.
fact.mars: Radio takes 3 to 22 minutes to cross between Earth and Mars, depending on orbits.

interludes.speaker: med
interludes.text: The crew is running on fumes. I'm prescribing 2 {Ds} of rest.
interludes.fact: Tired crews make mistakes. NASA plans astronaut sleep and time off carefully.

interludes.speaker: ls
interludes.text: The water recycler filter is clogging. Swapping it takes most of a {D}.
interludes.fact: The ISS recycles about 98% of its water, sweat and urine included.

interludes.speaker: arch

text.moon: Let's bury the habitat under regolith for radiation shielding. The diggers need 4 days.
text.mars: Let's pile Martian soil over the habitat to block radiation. It's 4 sols of digging.

interludes.fact: A couple of metres of packed soil can block much of the radiation from space.

interludes.speaker: cook
interludes.text: Fresh salad night! The crew would love it, but it eats into the harvest.
interludes.fact: In 2015, ISS astronauts ate lettuce grown in orbit in NASA's Veggie chamber.

text.moon: Schools on Earth want a live lesson from the Moon. With a 1.3-second delay, it'll feel almost real-time!
text.mars: Schools on Earth want a lesson from Mars. With a 12-minute delay it can't be live, so we'd record a Q&A.

fact.moon: Apollo TV broadcasts reached Earth with just over a second of delay.
fact.mars: A Mars crew can't chat live with Earth. Every reply takes minutes.

interludes.speaker: bot
interludes.text: I want to test a tough new potato strain. It's 3 {Ds} to plant, and it could boom… or bust.
interludes.fact: Potatoes are a top space crop: lots of calories from very little space.

interludes.speaker: ls
interludes.text: Oxygen reserves are thin. I can push the electrolysis unit, which splits water into oxygen.
interludes.fact: Electrolysis splits H₂O into hydrogen and oxygen. The ISS makes its air this way.

text.moon: The crew keeps staring at Earth through the window. A VR "beach day" might help.
text.mars: Earth is just a bright dot in the Martian sky now. The crew is homesick. VR beach day?

fact.moon: From the Moon, Earth looks nearly four times wider than the Moon does from Earth.
fact.mars: From Mars, Earth looks like a bright evening star, too small to see continents.

interludes.speaker: eng

text.moon: Clingy moondust is coating the solar panels. Someone has to suit up and brush it off.
text.mars: Red dust is choking the solar panels. Suit up and clean them?

interludes.fact: Every spacewalk adds radiation dose and risk, so each one is planned in detail.

text.moon: A lander leaves Earth soon, just a few days' flight away. Room for one priority: food or spare parts?
text.mars: The next cargo ship is months out and lands in about 8 sols. Food or spare parts?

fact.moon: Earth to the Moon takes about 3 days. Close enough for regular resupply.
fact.mars: Earth to Mars takes 6 to 9 months, so cargo must be planned far ahead.

interludes.speaker: bot
interludes.text: We could compost waste into fertilizer. Great for crops… the habitat will smell for days.
interludes.fact: Turning waste back into food and air is called "closing the loop." It's key far from Earth.

interludes.speaker: rook
interludes.text: Commander! I volunteer for a double shift to finish the battery repairs today!
interludes.fact: On real missions, safety beats speed. Overwork raises injury risk.

interludes.speaker: eng
interludes.text: A battery bank upgrade takes 3 {Ds}. It hurts now but pays off big.

fact.moon: Batteries must carry a lunar base through 14 days of darkness. That's a LOT of storage.
fact.mars: Batteries store solar power for the Martian night and for dusty days.

interludes.speaker: med

text.moon: In one-sixth gravity, the crew's bones and muscles are weakening. Make 2 hours of exercise mandatory?
text.mars: In Mars's 38% gravity, the crew's bones are weakening. Mandatory workouts?

interludes.fact: ISS astronauts exercise about 2 hours a day to protect bones and muscles.

interludes.speaker: sci
interludes.text: We have a huge science dataset for Earth. Sending it will hog the comms link for 2 {Ds}.
interludes.fact: NASA's Deep Space Network has giant antennas in California, Spain and Australia.

interludes.speaker: hq

text.moon: Four new colonists are ready. It's only a 3-day flight to the Moon. Accept them?
text.mars: Four colonists can join the next transfer, landing in about 8 sols. Accept them?

interludes.fact: More people means more hands, but also more air, water and food every single day.

interludes.speaker: ops
interludes.text: A micrometeoroid pinged the hull. Tiny leak. Patch it now or keep an eye on it?
interludes.fact: Micrometeoroids can travel many times faster than a bullet.

interludes.speaker: aria
interludes.text: I can automate greenhouse watering, Commander. It saves crew time but uses extra computing power.
interludes.fact: Robots and AI will handle many chores at future bases, freeing astronauts for science.

text.moon: It's Rookie Kim's birthday, the first one on the Moon! Bake a cake with the sugar reserve?
text.mars: It's Rookie Kim's birthday! Earth birthday or Mars birthday? Either way… cake?

fact.moon: Food is a big morale boost. Astronauts help pick their menus before launch.
fact.mars: One Mars year lasts 687 Earth days, so Mars birthdays come almost half as often.

text.moon: One lunar "day" lasts a whole Earth month. The crew's body clocks are confused. Install circadian lighting?
text.mars: A sol is 39 minutes longer than an Earth day. Switch the crew to Mars time?

fact.moon: The Moon spins once every 29.5 Earth days, so a lunar day lasts about two Earth weeks.
fact.mars: Mars rover teams on Earth work on "Mars time," shifting their schedule about 40 minutes a day.
